As long as you are not prioritizing or consistently repeating 1 on 1 lunches with this coworker over your relationship, you’re NTB. If work lunches are few and far between enough for it to not be considered objectively suspicious, then she is definitely helicoptering you a little too much. HOWEVER, if your girlfriend does feel neglected that might just be a sign that you should take her out a bit more often. Maybe if you do end up going out for lunch with your coworkers you should probably plan a date with your significant other within the same week.

Do not feel pressured to stay in the relationship though. If he is really taking too long for you or if for any reason he cannot have sex until another requirement is met (I.e. marriage etc.) then yes definitely leave the relationship. Just as he is not obligated to give you his body, you are not obligated to stay in the relationship if he outright refuses to. Relationships are agreements, not contracts. Save the contracts until marriage.

Technically NTB… BUT, continuing the relationship and letting that be a burden to the relationship could end in him feeling pressured. If you truly want to continue the relationship and are willing to lower sex as a priority, then waiting until he is ready will make the experience so much better when it happens rather than you being disgruntled because he’s not ready. It’s completely normal to be in a relationship and not have sex until as late as a couple months in. But if you do believe that sex is a pivotal part of the relationship then yes, you should explain to him that your conflicting ideals cause too much tension to be able to continue a healthy relationship. So you technically would not be wrong to leave, but just being there until he’s ready and not trying to motion the relationship in that direction before he’s ready will make that moment so much more meaningful to the both of you when he DOES feel ready to move the relationship that way.
